title: Standards you can keep, dignity for all, and a care notebook

say: Standards you can keep, dignity for every customer, and a simple care notebook.
This is the video for module three of Customer Care and Respectful Communication.
Good intentions fade on busy days. So in this module, you turn customer care into things you can check.

panel.heading: Good intentions fade on busy days

say: You will serve every customer with dignity, including those who are easy to overlook.

panel.heading: Good intentions fade on busy days

say: You will protect their information.

panel.heading: Good intentions fade on busy days

say: And you will keep a simple notebook that shows whether your care is improving.

panel.heading: Good intentions fade on busy days

say: A service standard is a promise about how you treat every customer, written so you can check it. We give good service cannot be checked.
We greet every customer within 10 seconds can be checked on any day.

Choose numbers you can keep on your busiest day, not your quietest. An honest 1-hour reply promise you always keep beats a 10-minute promise you break every market day. Five to seven standards are enough.
For example, Bisi runs a POS stand in Ilorin. Her customers complained about surprise charges, long waits when the network was slow, and confusion when transfers failed.

panel.heading: Standards for a POS stand
items: List your three most common complaints
Write one checkable standard for each
Check them at the end of the week

say: So she wrote: I say the charge before every transaction. If the network is down, I tell each waiting customer within 1 minute. If a transaction fails, I give the reference in writing and check with you the next day.

say: She added two more: greet every customer, and serve strictly in order of arrival, with priority for older customers and anyone with a disability.

say: After one week, she had announced 5 of 6 network failures within a minute. She circled the miss and wrote why.

say: Bank reversals are handled by the bank, not by Bisi. So she promises what she will do: tell, check and follow up.

panel.rule: Promise what you will do, not what others control

say: Respect is tested most with customers who are easy to overlook. Rule one: ask before you help. Would you like me to read the price list for you? Never grab a person's arm or wheelchair.

panel.heading: Ask, and speak to the customer
items: Speak to the customer, not the companion
Older customer: a seat and a slower pace
Deaf customer: face her, write or type
Cannot read: read terms aloud in private

say: Rule two: speak to the customer, not their companion. They are the one buying.

say: The Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 governs personal data. For you, that means: collect only what you need. Hide names and numbers before sharing any screenshot. Do not add customers to groups they did not agree to.
Never discuss one customer's debts with another. Never ask for a PIN or code. And keep your notebook and phone locked.

panel.heading: Customer information is not yours
items: Hide names and numbers in screenshots
Never discuss one customer with another
Never ask for a PIN or code
Keep your notebook and phone locked

say: You cannot improve what you only feel. An exercise book is enough. Write each entry straight after the conversation, first names only, and be honest in the kept column.

panel.heading: Count, then fix one thing
items: Choose one action for next month

say: For example, Amaka sells dresses in Owerri. She made 40 promises and kept 34. That is 85 percent.

panel.heading: Count, then fix one thing
items: Choose one action for next month

say: She had 8 complaints and resolved 6 the same day. That is 75 percent.

panel.heading: Count, then fix one thing
items: Choose one action for next month

say: Late delivery caused 4 of the 8 complaints, and all 6 broken promises were delivery dates.

panel.heading: Count, then fix one thing
items: Choose one action for next month

say: So she chose one action: add two extra days to every quoted date, and message customers the moment a job runs late. With small numbers, look at the counts too, and compare month to month.

panel.heading: Count, then fix one thing
items: Choose one action for next month

say: To remember. Write standards you can check and keep. Ask before you help. Treat everyone the same.
Protect customer information. And count your notebook each month, then fix one thing.

panel.heading: Remember
items: A standard is a promise you can check
Same price and patience for everyone
Count monthly and fix one thing
